extracted.title: Marked for Disruption: Tracing the Evolution of Malware Delivery Operations Targeted for Takedown
extracted.venue: arXiv 2104.01631 v3, 7 July 2021; the text states publication at RAID '21 (6 to 8 October 2021). Screened as an arXiv preprint on search metadata
extracted.inclusion: included (Part A): DNS sinkhole and seizure operations against three malware delivery operations in late 2015; outcome is the operations' download and network activity over the following year; method stated
extracted.population: global download metadata from a security vendor's product telemetry, October 2015 to September 2016
extracted.data_public: no: vendor telemetry; one author employed by the vendor
outcome_facts: "Dridex exhibits consistent growth in network activity during the DNS sinkhole, while Dorkbot and Upatre both exhibit significant, short-term drops in network activity after their respective takedowns with varying long-term responses" (Figure 2 caption)
One operation's network activity, after falling for several weeks after the takedown, was stable for months and then rose and fluctuated at a raised level from mid-April 2016 (Section 6)
extracted.safety_note: The paper describes how the operations responded; under the brief those behaviours and reasons are not restated, and no host or domain detail is kept.
